page-title.purpose: One per page; defines the route. Top-left of every screen.

card-title.purpose: Uppercase header on every card or panel; the constant rhythm element across screens.

body.purpose: Paragraph copy and table cell text. Single sans family, no decorative variants.

numeric.purpose: Scores, ranks, percentages, grades. Always tabular-nums for vertical alignment.

micro-label.purpose: Uppercase metadata: column headers, nav-section titles, stat-pill labels.

shadows.name: surface-lift
shadows.purpose: Sticky table headers and the brand-logo lozenge. Functional float, never decorative.

shadows.name: hover-lift
shadows.purpose: Reserved for elements you actively pick up: drag handles, popover anchors. Not for rest-state cards.

shadows.name: focus-glow
shadows.purpose: Focus-visible state on primary interactive elements. Doubles as keyboard-nav feedback.

motion.name: ease-fast
motion.purpose: Default transition for hover state changes (background, border, color).

motion.name: ease-bar
motion.purpose: Strength-bar width transition. The only data-driven motion in the system.

motion.name: ease-out-quart
motion.purpose: Default exponential ease-out for any new entrance animation. Never bounce, never elastic.

narrative.overview:
This is what a printed dynasty tier sheet would become if you let it watch your rosters. Surfaces stay close to the page (graphite-on-obsidian, no glassy noise, no decorative gradient), category color is the only flourish, and the only thing that ever moves is data. The reader is an analyst at a console mid-week, not a fan scrolling on the couch. Every screen is a working document; nothing performs.

The aesthetic explicitly rejects three things: Sleeper's mobile-first cartoon-mascot energy, ESPN/Yahoo's ad-shaped portal clutter, and the generic SaaS purple-gradient hero that signals 'AI-tool landing page.' Cornerstone Violet is a category, not a marketing accent. We do not paint it onto buttons for personality.
keyCharacteristics: Dark by default. The user is at a desk, mid-week, often at night.
Color is meaning. Every accent maps to a tier or a category. None are decoration.
Density over generosity. Tight rows, compact pills, monospace numbers, no card padding theatre.
Chrome disappears. Borders, shadows, and containers earn their place by separating real things.
Keyboard is the front door. Cmd+K is canonical, not an afterthought.

rules.name: The Three-Pillar Rule
rules.body: Cornerstone Violet, Foundational Sky, and Upside Mint are not three accents that happen to be close. They are the three category pillars. They appear as a triad together or alone with role-meaning. Never mix in a fourth pillar color.

rules.name: The No-Decorative-Color Rule
rules.body: If a hue appears on screen, it is communicating a category or a tier. There is no 'we needed something to break up the gray.' Break up the gray with hierarchy and density, not paint.

rules.name: The Anti-Gradient Rule
rules.body: Two gradients exist in the system: the brand-logo lozenge and the team-strength bar. Both encode the pillar pairing. Do not introduce a third.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Anything quantitative renders in tabular-nums. Stats, scores, pick numbers, percentages, grades, ranks, ages. Non-tabular numbers in a tier sheet are visual chaos.

rules.name: The Uppercase-as-Metadata Rule
rules.body: ALL CAPS is reserved for labels about the data, never for the data itself. Card titles, column headers, nav sections — yes. Player names, team names, body copy — never.

rules.name: The 65–75ch Rule
rules.body: Body copy never exceeds 75 characters per line. Long-form prose caps at 65–75ch even if the parent grid is wider.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Cards, rows, and panels at rest have no drop shadow. Their separation is the tonal step. If you reach for box-shadow on a static card, you wanted a tonal step instead.

rules.name: The Functional-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow answers a functional question — am I sticky, am I focused, am I being picked up? Decorative ambient shadows under cards are forbidden.

dos: Do make tabular-nums the default for any column with numbers. Scores, ranks, ages, percentages, grades all line up vertically.
Do use Cornerstone Violet for 'this is yours' cues across league tables and roster views — the 'you' row tint, the active nav stripe, the focus ring. The user is the violet thread through the data.
Do pair every tier color with the tier letter (S/A/B/C/D) at full opacity. Color-blind users get the letter; everyone else gets reinforcement.
Do lean on the tonal ramp (Obsidian → Graphite → Slate → Pewter) for elevation before reaching for a shadow. Shadows are state, not chrome.
Do keep the brand-mark gradient and the strength-bar gradient as the only gradients in the product. Both encode the Cornerstone+Foundational pillar pairing.
Do prefer OKLCH when introducing new colors; the existing hex palette is grandfathered.
Do make Cmd+K discoverable on every page (the small ⌘K chip in the page header).
donts: Don't use a colored side-stripe (border-left / border-right > 1px) as a card or list-item accent. The only inset stripe is the active sidebar nav item.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text over a gradient). Emphasis is weight or size, never a multicolor fill.
Don't apply glassmorphism, backdrop-blur surfaces, or frosted panels.
Don't introduce a fourth pillar color or invent a 'warning purple' / 'info purple' — Cornerstone Violet is one thing.
Don't add a hero metric template (big number + small label + supporting stats + gradient flourish).
Don't add bounce, elastic, spring, or scale-in animations. Ease out exponentially.
Don't use em dashes anywhere. Use commas, colons, or periods.
Don't make this look like Sleeper. No mobile-first layouts forcing themselves onto desktop, no mascot iconography.
Don't make this look like ESPN/Yahoo. No ad-shaped containers, no ticker-tape strips.
Don't make this look like a generic SaaS landing page. No purple-to-blue marketing gradient hero.
Don't wrap every section in a container. Most rows don't need one.
Don't nest cards inside cards. If a section feels like it needs a sub-card, the outer card should be a layout region instead.
